description: Join The Rutgers Democracy Lab for their first-ever Welcome Bash. Get a bite to eat at a food truck, check if you are registered to vote with our RU Voting Team, play some games and win a prize, learn about what the programs at RDL are up to this semester, or take a ride on the bumper cars. Students can also add to the chain of pledges to vote, get an ice cream sundae, write on our democracy wall, take pictures at our photo booth, or try their hand at human shuffleboard. Come with friends or be ready to make new ones to see what other surprises RDL has in store. All students are welcome to this free event.
name: Welcome Week RDL Welcome Bash
organizationName: The Rutgers Democracy Lab at the Eagleton Institute of Politics

description: HOSA is hosting our first general information session of the year, followed by speed friending. Free refreshments and snacks will be provided. Excited to meet you all!🩺😁
name: Speed Friending and Sweets

description: We aim to bring an inclusive and supportive community for people with interest in learning how to solve Rubik’s cubes and enhancing their skills with various other types of puzzles to learn what it is like to become competitive. We also plan to organize competitions at the school.
name: First Rubik's Cube Club Meeting

description: This Welcome Weeks event is an opportunity for students, both international and domestic, to learn about all that Rutgers Global has to offer: advising for international students, study abroad opportunities, on-campus programming, and more. There will be a tie-dye (free t-shirts!), games, prizes, and lots of food.   Please note the rain date for this event will be Thursday, September 10 (same times)   This event is also listed on The Arc / the Suitable app.  Learn more about The Arc here.
name: Rutgers Global Expo

description: Welcome Home! Join us at SJE for our annual LGBTQIA+ Grad Student Welcome! Mingle and connect with your master’s and doctoral peers while enjoying good food and music.    This event is in partnership with BIPOC LGBTQIA2S+ Graduate Affinity Group, GRADient, and Graduate Student Life.
location: Center for Social Justice Education & LGBT Communities
name: LGBTQIA+ Grad Student Welcome
organizationName: Center for Social Justice Education and LGBT Communities (Rutgers University)

description: As a follow-up to his Constitution Day conversation, students are invited to engage in a discussion with Constitutional Scholar and Yale Professor Akhil Amar. The discussion will be facilitated by Talking Across Diggerenece Student Leaders.   Breakfast will be provided to registered students.  Open to all current students.  click here to register
name: Continuing the Conversation: a Student Discussion with Professor Akhil Amar

description: Wondering about accommodations? Know how to implement accommodations? Just want to visit with friends over coffee and donuts? The Office of Disability Services (ODS) is hosting an open house for undergraduate and graduate students with disabilities and disability allies. Food and beverages while supplies last.   Please register in advance.   Questions or accommodation requests specific to this event? Please email dsoffice@echo.rutgers.edu, call 848-202-3111, or visit ODS in Lucy Stone Hall, Suite A145, Livingston Campus.
location: Lucy Stone Hall, 1st Floor Lobby, Suite A145, Livingston Campus
name: Donuts and Drop In! ODS & Friends

description: Join us in celebrating our first-year students as they complete their 1st exam! Come grab free pizza on Monday, September 21st, from 12:45 - 2 pm in the RWJMS Research Tower, Dean’s Conference Room, Room 123, 675 Hoes Lane West, Piscataway
name: First Exam Pizza Party

description: Let’s Talk With Art Take a break, get creative, and connect.   Let’s Talk With Art is a relaxed, welcoming space for students to explore thoughts, feelings, and experiences through creativity. No artistic experience is needed. Come as you are and use whatever form of expression feels right for you, including drawing, painting, writing, collage, or simply experimenting with something new.   CAPS counselors will be creating alongside you, painting, drawing, and participating in the space with students. They are also available if you want to check in, talk something through, ask a question, or have a more personal conversation during the event.   Each session includes optional creative prompts, space for reflection, and opportunities for conversation and connection. You are also welcome to create independently and participate at your own comfort level.   Art can give us another way to express what may be hard to put into words, slow down, and check in with ourselves.   Fall 2026 Dates:October 1October 15November 5November 19December 3 Join us for one session or come back throughout the semester.
name: Let’s Talk With Art
organizationName: Counseling, Alcohol and Other Drug Assistance Program & Psychiatric Services (University Department)
organizationNames: Counseling, Alcohol and Other Drug Assistance Program & Psychiatric Services (University Department)
Scarlet Arts Rx (Affiliated with a Mason Gross School of the Arts Department)

name: Community Conversation
organizationName: Tyler Clementi Center for Diversity Education and Bias Prevention - TCC (University Department)
